classification.difficultyReason: Plot supplied coordinate pairs, label the four curves and connect their relative widths to the coefficient of x²; completed tables and fixed axes scaffold the comparison.

content.prompt: Plot these on the same axis and label each parabola.

spec.description: Editable blank student grid with the source axes, ranges and ticks; the completed curve is retained in the answer diagram.
spec.mathematics: y=2x^2, y=x^2, y=x^2/2 and y=x^2/4, all with vertex (0,0); x ticks -6 to 6, y ticks -1 to 19, zero omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: The task requires students to draw the curve. Completed curves belong to solution diagrams; given graphs for reading, identification and matching are retained.

answer.worked: Plot each table's coordinate pairs and join each set with a smooth curve. All four curves have vertex $(0,0)$. From the plotted curves, label the parabolas from narrowest to widest as $y=2x^2$, $y=x^2$, $y=\frac12x^2$ and $y=\frac14x^2$.

spec.description: Complete common-axis plot with a two-row standard-palette colour legend identifying all four parabolas without squeezing the unit grid.
spec.mathematics: Four parabolas y=2x^2, y=x^2, y=x^2/2 and y=x^2/4 on the source unit grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer-only equation labels identify all four curves.

answer.worked: For these positive coefficients, increasing the coefficient of $x^2$ makes the curve rise more steeply on each side of the vertex, so the parabola becomes narrower. Correct answer: B.
